title: How RECLAIM works
summary: Assess, build your Blueprint, train and eat to it, add clinician-led care only where appropriate, and measure what changes.

cues.text: RECLAIM starts with an assessment of your goals, your schedule, how you move today and what has got in the way before.
That becomes your Blueprint: a written plan for training, nutrition, sleep and habits that fits the week you actually have.
Your coach turns the Blueprint into weekly sessions you can do at home, in a partner gym or with a trainer.
If you ask for it, an independent clinician reviews whether medical care is appropriate. The clinician decides, not the programme.
We re-measure strength, body composition and habits on a schedule, and adjust the plan to what the data shows.

title: What happens in a Blueprint session
summary: A 60-minute session with a coach that turns your assessment into a plan with measurable targets.

cues.text: Before your session you complete a short questionnaire. Nothing you enter is shared with anyone until you create an account.
Your coach walks you through simple baseline tests, such as a 30-second sit-to-stand and a timed walk, adapted to any pain or limits.
You leave with a four-week plan, three measurable targets and a date for your first re-check.

title: 30-second sit-to-stand test
summary: How to run the baseline leg-strength test safely at home.

cues.text: Use a sturdy chair against a wall. Sit in the middle of the seat, feet flat, arms crossed over your chest.
On go, stand fully and sit fully as many times as you can in 30 seconds. Stop if you feel pain or dizziness.
Log the number of full stands in Progress. We repeat this test every four weeks.

title: Goblet squat: technique
summary: The foundation lower-body pattern in most RECLAIM plans, with regressions.

cues.text: Hold one weight at your chest with elbows pointing down. Feet a little wider than hips, toes slightly out.
Sit down between your heels, keeping your chest tall. Go only as deep as you can without pain, then drive up.
If this is too much today, squat to a chair or a box. Depth comes with practice.

title: Hip hinge: dowel drill
summary: Learn to bend from the hips, the basis of deadlifts and safe lifting at home.

cues.text: Hold a broomstick along your spine so it touches the back of your head, upper back and tailbone.
Soften the knees and push your hips back. Keep all three points touching the stick as you bend and return.

title: Incline push-up progression
summary: Build upper-body strength from wall push-ups to the floor.

cues.text: Hands on the wall at shoulder height. Keep a straight line from head to heels as you lower and press away.
When three sets of twelve feel easy, move your hands to a kitchen counter and repeat.
Progress one step lower at a time. Your coach will update your plan when you log the reps.

title: Lesson 1: Protein, simply
summary: Why protein matters when you are trying to change body composition, and how to spread it across the day.

cues.text: When you eat less, some of the weight you lose can be muscle. Enough protein and regular strength training help you keep it.
Your Blueprint sets a daily protein target based on your body size and your clinician's guidance where relevant.
Aim to include a palm-sized protein portion at each meal rather than saving it all for dinner.

title: Lesson 2: Sleep and appetite
summary: How short sleep changes hunger, and three changes that make the biggest difference.

cues.text: In controlled studies, restricting sleep increased hunger and, during dieting, shifted weight loss away from fat and toward lean tissue.
Keep a consistent wake time, dim screens for the last hour, and log your sleep so your coach can see the pattern.

title: Lesson 3: Plateaus are data
summary: What a stall on the scale does and does not mean, and what we look at instead.

cues.text: Day-to-day weight moves with water, salt and digestion. A flat week is common and rarely means the plan has failed.
We look at the trend, your waist measurement, your strength tests and your adherence before changing anything.
